newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks fall on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks fall on profit taking.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks tumbled Wednesday as investors called time out after a spirited rally on the Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates unchanged.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 57.75 points at 7,245.71 following Tuesday's 75-point surge after the Fed's decision.
Early in the session, the Dow romped ahead nearly 50 points, but profit-taking ate into the rally as bonds headed lower.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a slim margin on active volume of 342 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
"We rose in a straight line for a long time, so it's normal to see consolidation," said Frank Calta, a trader for Dain Bosworth.
Stocks were distracted by a sell-off in bonds, knocked lower by data that showed the U.S. trade gap narrowed by 19.3 percent in March to $8.5 billion.
The smaller deficit, which was well below Wall Street economists' forecasts of a $10.3 billion March shortfall, was attributed to record exports.
Analysts said the March trade figure would prompt economists to raise their estimates for Gross Domestic Product growth in the first quarter.
"The trade data is a factor for stock markets because, clearly, inflation can come from this area," said Ray Hirsch, director of the technology group at American Express Financial Advisors.
In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond fell 27/32, which raised its yield to 6.97 percent from 6.90 percent at Tuesday's close. Prices and yields move in opposite directions.
On Tuesday, the Fed kept interest rates unchanged in hopes that the economy will slow from its recent break-neck pace.

The economy grew at a 5.6 percent annualized clip in the first quarter, its fastest pace in more than nine years. But inflation has remained quiescent, with consumer prices rising at a year-on-year rate of 2.5 percent in April.

Hirsch said the bond market was more nervous about future inflation than the stock market, and perhaps had a predilection to weaken because they would have preferred to see the Fed boost interest rates to keep future inflation in check.
Ron Doran, head of institutional equity trading at C.L. King & Associates, said the stock market was overbought and prone to more profit-taking over the next few days.
"From now on investors will focus on economic data as it comes out and earnings," he said. "But for the short-term, the market is overbought."
Meanwhile, the Nasdaq composite index rose 8.17 points to 1,372.05, boosted by strong quarterly earnings from Dell Computer Corp., which gained 7-7/8 to 107-1/2.
The rally extended to computer companies. Compaq Computer Corp. was up 6 to 102-1/4 while Gateway 2000 Inc. added 3-3/8 to trade at 74-1/2.
Among other active issues, Keystone shares jumped 10-5/8 to 31-1/8 on news that Tyco International Inc. will acquire the company for about $1.2 billion in stock. Tyco was off 1-1/8 at 61-5/8.
Harnischfeger Industries said its earnings for the current fiscal year would fall short of analysts' expectations and its stock lost 4-1/8 to 38-7/8.
